title: Pakistan and the Maldives sign 20 agreements
credits: Photos: Ishan @seefromthesky, Ahmed Naahil, Shifaaz shamoon, Pedro Bariak / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: For the first time in eleven years, a president of the Maldives is on a state visit to Pakistan.
President Mohamed Muizzu arrived in Islamabad on the twentieth of October, for a three-day visit.
The trip also marks sixty years of diplomatic relations, which began in nineteen sixty-six.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Muizzu oversaw the exchange of twenty memorandums of understanding.
They cover IT and cybersecurity, health, defence, maritime security, fisheries, tourism, education and much more.
Field Marshal Asim Munir called on President Muizzu, and both sides stressed stronger defence cooperation.
Trade between the two countries is tiny today, at around fourteen million dollars a year.
The leaders want to raise it to two hundred million dollars within two years.
About two hundred and fifty Pakistani doctors and paramedics already work in the Maldives.
Pakistan will also send one hundred thousand olive cuttings, for the Maldives' plan to plant five million trees.
The Maldives is made up of around twelve hundred coral islands, spread across the Indian Ocean.
